group: Med Benthic Carnivores | Small Benthic Carnivores | Large Benthic Carnivores
explanation: Unidentified-finfish aggregate that Sea Around Us classes as Medium demersals (30 - 89 cm), so it is apportioned across the model's three demersal-carnivore groups, whose members in the Bulletin 51 components-of-ecological-groupings table (PDF pp. 21-22) span exactly that band and its neighbours (Small Benthic Carnivores mean L-inf 23 cm, Med Benthic Carnivores 35 cm, Large Benthic Carnivores 55 cm). Deliberately excluded: Large Pelagics, Tunas, Sharks, Skates & Rays, Marine Mammals and all invertebrate groups (wrong habitat or wrong phylum); Mackerel, Clupeids and Anchovies (small-pelagic groups, against the demersal class); the benthopelagic groups (different habitat); and Benthic Omnivores, whose fish members - soles, eel catfish, cornetfish - are all separately identified in this LME's catch and which is a detritivore rather than a carnivore compartment. Weighted by the catch composition of the identified taxa already on the three groups.

Member 62 of Grp13 Clupeids in the Bulletin 51 components-of-ecological-groupings table (PDF pp. 21-22); the group account calls the oil sardine the abundant species of the group and tabulates its L-inf, P/B and Q/B.

Grp16 Shrimps in the Bulletin 51 components-of-ecological-groupings table (PDF pp. 21-22) is built on the penaeid genera Metapenaeus, Parapenaeopsis and Trachypenaeus, plus the related Solenocera and Aristeus; the family is contained in the group and the model has no other shrimp compartment.
The sole member (61) of Grp12 Mackerel in the Bulletin 51 components-of-ecological-groupings table (PDF pp. 21-22); the group account is written entirely about this species.

The Bulletin's ecological-grouping paragraph defines Med Benthic Carnivores as 'sciaenids, flatheads, bull's eye, pomfrets, balistids, flounders', and the Bulletin 51 components-of-ecological-groupings table (PDF pp. 21-22) lists Johnieops sina (35) and Otolithes ruber (36) there.

Order-level crustacean record. The model holds decapods in exactly two groups - Crabs & Lobster (Portunus, Charybdis, Panulirus) and Shrimps (Metapenaeus, Parapenaeopsis, Solenocera, Trachypenaeus, Aristeus, Acetes) per the Bulletin 51 components-of-ecological-groupings table (PDF pp. 21-22) - so the split is over those two. Excluded: Heterotrophic Benthos, whose 'benthic crabs' are the unlanded epifaunal component, and Benthic Omnivores, whose crustacean member Oratosquilla is a stomatopod, not a decapod. Sea Around Us classes the record as functional group Lobsters, crabs while the catch-composition basis leans to Shrimps because this LME's identified crustacean landings are shrimp-dominated; the two signals disagree, and a reviewer may prefer explicit crab-weighted shares. The catch-composition basis was kept because it uses this ecosystem's own data and because the two groups' SPPR differ by only about a third, so the split is not load-bearing.

Bombay-duck; not named anywhere in the Bulletin, whose Karnataka species list does not include it. Placed with its closest listed relatives, the lizardfishes Saurida tumbil and S. undosquamis (Aulopiformes) in Grp8 Large Benthic Carnivores, on the strength of the shared order, the shared ambush-piscivore habit and a group TL of 4.14 against this record's 4.20. A reviewer could argue for Large Benthopelagics on the Sea Around Us benthopelagic class; the two groups' TLs are within 0.01 of each other but their SPPR differ, so this is the largest single-taxon judgement call in the file (3.2 % of tonnage).

Order-level record classed by Sea Around Us as Small pelagics (<30 cm). The model splits clupeiforms between Clupeids (Sardinella spp., Thryssa mystax, Dussumieria, Escualosa, Pellona, Opisthopterus) and Anchovies (Stolephorus spp.) per the Bulletin 51 components-of-ecological-groupings table (PDF pp. 21-22), so the record is apportioned over those two. The third clupeiform placement in the model, the wolf herring Chirocentrus dorab in Large Benthopelagics, is excluded because it is a >90 cm fish against a small-pelagic class and Chirocentrus is separately identified in this catch. Weighted by the catch composition of the identified clupeiforms, which is dominated by the oil sardine.

Grp10 Small Benthic Carnivores in the Bulletin 51 components-of-ecological-groupings table (PDF pp. 21-22) lists Nemipterus japonicus (46) and N. mesoprion (47), and the group account leads with 'threadfin breams'; the family is contained in the group.

Grp13 Clupeids in the Bulletin 51 components-of-ecological-groupings table (PDF pp. 21-22) is the model's clupeid pool - Sardinella spp., Dussumieria acuta, Escualosa thoracata, Pellona and Opisthopterus - so the family is contained in it.

'Bivalves' is member 89 of Grp18 Heterotrophic Benthos in the Bulletin 51 components-of-ecological-groupings table (PDF pp. 21-22), and the group account (PDF p. 30) defines the group as the benthic epifauna of bivalves, gastropods, echinoderms, benthic crabs, amphipods and isopods.

The Bulletin's ecological-grouping paragraph defines Small Benthopelagics as 'scads, carangids, moonfish and myctophids', so a residual carangid record belongs there. Not split, although the model does place three carangids elsewhere - Megalaspis cordyla and Scomberoides tol in Large Benthopelagics and Parastromateus niger in Med Benthic Carnivores - because all three are separately and substantially identified in this LME's catch, and because the catch on Large Benthopelagics is about two-thirds sea catfish, so a catch-composition split would be set by non-carangid tonnage.
Member 11 of Grp4 Large Pelagics in the Bulletin 51 components-of-ecological-groupings table (PDF pp. 21-22); the group account names it first and tabulates its L-inf, P/B, aspect ratio and Q/B.

Grp5 Tunas in the Bulletin 51 components-of-ecological-groupings table (PDF pp. 21-22) is Euthynnus affinis, Thunnus tonggol, Auxis thazard and A. rochei; the genus Thunnus is a listed member genus and the model has no other tuna compartment.

Three of the four members of Grp2 Sharks in the Bulletin 51 components-of-ecological-groupings table (PDF pp. 21-22) - Rhizoprionodon acutus, Carcharhinus limbatus, Scoliodon laticaudus - are carcharhinids, and the model's only other elasmobranch group is batoid.

Member 28 of Grp7 Large Benthopelagics in the Bulletin 51 components-of-ecological-groupings table (PDF pp. 21-22) is 'Tachysurus sp.', an ariid sea catfish, and the group account names catfish among the group's five constituents.

Subclass-level record spanning both of the model's elasmobranch groups, which are split cleanly into true sharks (Rhizoprionodon, Carcharhinus, Scoliodon, Sphyrna) and batoids (Rhinobatos, Rhinoptera, Dasyatis) in the Bulletin 51 components-of-ecological-groupings table (PDF pp. 21-22). Apportioned by the catch composition of the identified elasmobranchs of this LME, which leans to sharks and so agrees with the Sea Around Us class of Large sharks (>=90 cm).

Order-level catfish record. Marine Siluriformes landings on this coast are effectively all Ariidae, which the model places in Grp7 Large Benthopelagics as 'Tachysurus sp.' (the Bulletin 51 components-of-ecological-groupings table (PDF pp. 21-22)). Not split against the model's only other siluriform, the eel catfish Plotosus in Benthic Omnivores: Plotosidae is a negligible component of the landings here (507 t against 2.3 Mt for this record), and catch-composition weights over the two groups would give it a quarter of the record.

Netuma thalassina is the accepted name of Arius/Tachysurus thalassinus; 'Tachysurus sp.' is member 28 of Grp7 Large Benthopelagics in the Bulletin 51 components-of-ecological-groupings table (PDF pp. 21-22).

CORRECTION to the inherited mapping. The silverbellies Leiognathus bindus and Secutor insidiator are members 51 and 50 of Grp10 Small Benthic Carnivores in the Bulletin 51 components-of-ecological-groupings table (PDF pp. 21-22), and the group account (PDF p. 27) names silverbellies among its dominant species with life-history rows for both. The family was previously mapped to Small Benthopelagics, a group whose SPPR is about fifteen times higher.

Decapterus russelli (56) and D. macrosoma (57) are members of Grp11 Small Benthopelagics in the Bulletin 51 components-of-ecological-groupings table (PDF pp. 21-22) and the two species the group account parameterises.

Grp14 Anchovies in the Bulletin 51 components-of-ecological-groupings table (PDF pp. 21-22) is Stolephorus devisi, S. waitei, S. commersonii and S. indicus plus the unicorn cod Bregmaceros mcclellandi. Not split against Clupeids, into which the Bulletin puts the engraulid Thryssa mystax, because Thryssa is separately identified in this catch and because Clupeids carries the oil sardine's 21.9 Mt, so a catch-composition split would put over 90 % of an anchovy record onto the sardine group.
Grp12 Mackerel in the Bulletin 51 components-of-ecological-groupings table (PDF pp. 21-22) is the single species Rastrelliger kanagurta, so the genus record is contained in the group.

group: Med Benthic Carnivores | Small Benthic Carnivores | Large Benthic Carnivores
explanation: Order-level record classed by Sea Around Us as Medium demersals (30 - 89 cm) and commercial group Perch-likes. Perciform members of this model sit in the three demersal-carnivore groups (sciaenids, flatheads, pomfrets, bull's eye and threadfins in Med Benthic Carnivores; threadfin breams, terapons, whitefish, silverbellies, goatfishes and cardinalfish in Small Benthic Carnivores; rock cods, jobfish and snappers in Large Benthic Carnivores per the Bulletin 51 components-of-ecological-groupings table (PDF pp. 21-22)), so the record is apportioned over those three. Excluded: Mackerel (a single species, Rastrelliger kanagurta, separately and fully identified in this catch), Tunas and Large Pelagics (the demersal class rules them out and their perciform members are identified to genus here), the benthopelagic groups (different habitat) and Benthic Omnivores (its fish are soles, eel catfish and cornetfish - no perciforms).

The Bulletin's ecological-grouping paragraph defines Benthic Omnivores as 'soles, cornetfish, squilla', and the Bulletin 51 components-of-ecological-groupings table (PDF pp. 21-22) lists the Malabar sole Cynoglossus macrostomus (85) there; the group account describes it as a detritus feeder. The model's flounders (Pseudorhombus) sit in Med Benthic Carnivores instead, so this is a feeding-mode split within the flatfishes, not a taxonomic one.

Grp6 Cephalopods in the Bulletin 51 components-of-ecological-groupings table (PDF pp. 21-22) (Loligo duvauceli, Sepia pharaonis, S. elliptica, Sepiella inermis) is the model's only cephalopod compartment, so the class record is contained in it.
Stolephorus devisi (70), S. waitei (71), S. commersonii (72) and S. indicus (73) are the fish members of Grp14 Anchovies in the Bulletin 51 components-of-ecological-groupings table (PDF pp. 21-22).

Penaeidae, the family of Grp16's listed genera Metapenaeus, Parapenaeopsis and Trachypenaeus (the Bulletin 51 components-of-ecological-groupings table (PDF pp. 21-22)); the model has no other shrimp compartment.

Member 24 of Grp7 Large Benthopelagics in the Bulletin 51 components-of-ecological-groupings table (PDF pp. 21-22); the group account names 'Ribbonfish (Trichiurus lepturus)' first and tabulates its parameters.
Sepia pharaonis (21) and S. elliptica (22) are members of Grp6 Cephalopods in the Bulletin 51 components-of-ecological-groupings table (PDF pp. 21-22); the family is contained in the group.

Epinephelus diacanthus (29) and 'Serranus sp.' (33) are members of Grp8 Large Benthic Carnivores in the Bulletin 51 components-of-ecological-groupings table (PDF pp. 21-22), and the group account names 'rock cod (Epinephelus diacanthus)' as dominant.

Thryssa mystax is member 65 of Grp13 Clupeids in the Bulletin 51 components-of-ecological-groupings table (PDF pp. 21-22) - the Bulletin places this engraulid genus with the sardines, not in its Anchovies group, and the group account discusses Thryssa mystax's diet under Clupeids.

Grp5 Tunas in the Bulletin 51 components-of-ecological-groupings table (PDF pp. 21-22) is the model's Thunnini pool (Euthynnus, Thunnus, Auxis); Katsuwonus is a member of that tribe and the model has no other tuna compartment.

Saurida tumbil (31) and S. undosquamis (32) are members of Grp8 Large Benthic Carnivores in the Bulletin 51 components-of-ecological-groupings table (PDF pp. 21-22); the group account describes the lizardfishes' diet as part of the group.
Member 36 of Grp9 Med Benthic Carnivores in the Bulletin 51 components-of-ecological-groupings table (PDF pp. 21-22); the group account gives its diet composition.
Member 17 of Grp5 Tunas in the Bulletin 51 components-of-ecological-groupings table (PDF pp. 21-22); the group account tabulates its L-inf, P/B, aspect ratio and Q/B.

Family-level record classed by Sea Around Us as Medium pelagics (30 - 89 cm). The model distributes scombrids over exactly three groups - Mackerel (Rastrelliger kanagurta), Tunas (Euthynnus, Thunnus, Auxis) and Large Pelagics (the seerfishes Scomberomorus commerson and S. guttatus) per the Bulletin 51 components-of-ecological-groupings table (PDF pp. 21-22) - so the record is apportioned over those three and nothing else. Reviewer caveat: Sea Around Us gives this record commercial group Perch-likes rather than Tuna & billfishes, which hints the pile leans to Rastrelliger and Scomberomorus, and the three groups' SPPR differ by two orders of magnitude (Mackerel is modelled at TL 2.0 on an 88 % diatom diet), so this split is the single most consequential judgement in the file.
Squid order; Cephalopods is the model's only cephalopod-type group, so every cephalopod taxon is an unambiguous fit regardless of exact rank.
Blue swimming crab; exact genus (Portunus) explicitly named in Table 1's Crabs and lobsters definition.

Common dolphinfish; not one of Table 1's named examples, but ecologically a fast, large epipelagic piscivore matching this apex-predator group's diet (feeds on Mackerel/Clupeids/Anchovies groups per the diet matrix) and TL band (4.37-4.49 vs group TL 4.18).

Mullet family; mullets (Mugilidae) are benthic detritivore/omnivore grazers, not named in Table 1 but ecologically and trophically (TL 2.14-2.63) closest to the low-TL Benthic Omnivores guild (group TL 2.55).
Hilsa shad; Clupeidae, the family that itself defines the Clupeids group.

Longnose trevally; Carangidae, but a large apex predatory reef jack/trevally (TL 3.8-4.5) rather than the small schooling "scad" niche Table 1 names for Carangidae under Small Benthopelagics - placed instead with the demersal apex-predator guild (Large Benthic Carnivores) by size, diet and TL.

Bigeye thresher; Lamniformes true shark. This model splits sharks from batoids cleanly (group 2 vs group 3), and any true-shark genus not a batoid is an unambiguous fit to Sharks even where the exact genus is not one of Table 1's named examples (Rhizoprionodon, Carcharhinus, Scoliodon, Sphyrna).

CORRECTION to the inherited mapping. Listed as 'Formio niger', member 39 of Grp9 Med Benthic Carnivores in the Bulletin 51 components-of-ecological-groupings table (PDF pp. 21-22); Formio is a junior synonym of Parastromateus, and the group account (PDF p. 27) names 'Black pomfret (Parastromateus niger)' and tabulates its L-inf, P/B and Q/B. Previously mapped to Small Benthopelagics.
Shortfin mako; Lamnidae true shark (mackerel shark family), unambiguous fit to the model's single Sharks group under the clean shark/batoid split.
Indo-Pacific king mackerel; exact genus (Scomberomorus = "seers, kingfish") explicitly named in Table 1's Large Pelagics definition.

CORRECTION to the inherited mapping. Member 49 of Grp10 Small Benthic Carnivores in the Bulletin 51 components-of-ecological-groupings table (PDF pp. 21-22); the group account names 'whitefish (Lactarius lactarius)' among its dominant species and gives it a life-history row. Previously mapped to Large Benthopelagics, a group whose SPPR is more than twenty times higher.
Seabream family; Sparidae, a benthic durophagous-invertivore guild not named in Table 1, placed with Med Benthic Carnivores by TL match (~3.3-3.5 vs group TL 3.19).
Talang queenfish; exact genus (Scomberoides = "queenfish") explicitly named in Table 1's Large Benthopelagics definition.
Great barracuda; exact genus (Sphyraena = "barracudas") explicitly named in Table 1's Large Pelagics definition.

Spangled emperor; Lethrinidae (emperor family), a demersal durophagous/piscivorous carnivore guild not named in Table 1 but ecologically parallel to the snapper/grouper apex reef-predator guild of Large Benthic Carnivores (mean TL ~3.7, group TL 4.14).

Emperor family; Lethrinidae (emperor family), a demersal durophagous/piscivorous carnivore guild not named in Table 1 but ecologically parallel to the snapper/grouper apex reef-predator guild of Large Benthic Carnivores (mean TL ~3.7, group TL 4.14).
Sind sardinella; "lesser sardines" (Sardinella spp) is Table 1's explicit example for Clupeids.
Barracuda genus explicitly named in Table 1's Large Pelagics definition ("seers, kingfish and barracudas").
True jellyfish class; "jellyfish" is Table 1's explicit example for Micro-nekton.
Kawakawa; exact genus (Euthynnus) explicitly named in Table 1's Tunas definition.
Suborder containing all penaeid shrimp; Shrimps is the model's only shrimp-type group, so this is an unambiguous fit.

Unidentified pelagic-finfish aggregate classed by Sea Around Us as Medium pelagics (30 - 89 cm). Apportioned across the model's four small-to-medium pelagic and benthopelagic finfish groups - Clupeids, Anchovies, Mackerel and Small Benthopelagics (scads, carangids, moonfish, myctophids) per the Bulletin 51 components-of-ecological-groupings table (PDF pp. 21-22). Excluded: Large Pelagics and Tunas (>90 cm groups whose members are identified to genus or species throughout this catch), Large Benthopelagics (its members are 46-125 cm catfish, ribbonfish and wolf herrings), all demersal-carnivore groups (wrong habitat), and Micro Nekton (a jellyfish-and-larvae compartment).
Pomfret (genus); "pomfrets" (Stromateidae, genus Pampus) is Table 1's explicit example for Med Benthic Carnivores.

Pomfret (Bramidae) family; not Table 1's Stromateidae "pomfrets" (which map to Med Benthic Carnivores) but a distinct, oceanic mid-water predatory family - placed here by TL match (group TL 4.15) and offshore benthopelagic habit rather than by the shared common name.
Doublespotted queenfish; exact genus (Scomberoides = "queenfish") explicitly named in Table 1's Large Benthopelagics definition.
Japanese threadfin bream; Nemipteridae (threadfin bream/monocle bream family) - "threadfin breams" is Table 1's explicit example for Small Benthic Carnivores.

Dussumier's thryssa; Table 1 explicitly names "Thryssa" under Clupeids (group 13), not under Anchovies (group 14, which names only Stolephorus and Bregmaceros mcclellandi) - an explicit, paper-stated exception to the usual Engraulidae=anchovy grouping, followed here as printed.
Striped piggy; Haemulidae (grunt/sweetlips family), a demersal benthic-invertivore guild not named in Table 1, placed with Med Benthic Carnivores by ecology and TL (~3.3-4.0 vs group TL 3.19).
Grouper (genus); Serranidae (grouper/rockcod family) - "rock cods" is Table 1's explicit example for Large Benthic Carnivores.
Goatfish family; "goatfishes" (Mullidae) is Table 1's explicit example for Small Benthic Carnivores.

Rabbitfish family; rabbitfish (Siganidae) are herbivorous reef grazers (TL ~2.0-2.76), not named in Table 1 but ecologically closest to the low-TL grazer/omnivore guild of Benthic Omnivores (group TL 2.55).
Bloch's gizzard shad; Clupeidae, the family that itself defines the Clupeids group.
Queenfish genus explicitly named in Table 1's Large Benthopelagics definition.
Cuttlefish (genus); Cephalopods is the model's only cephalopod-type group, so every cephalopod taxon is an unambiguous fit regardless of exact rank.
Wolf herring genus explicitly named in Table 1's Large Benthopelagics definition.
Eagle/manta ray family (batoid); any ray/skate family besides the shark side of the split is an unambiguous fit to Skates & Rays.
Pharaoh cuttlefish; Cephalopods is the model's only cephalopod-type group, so every cephalopod taxon is an unambiguous fit regardless of exact rank.

Threadfin family; unidentified-species entry with TL 3.62, closest to Med Benthic Carnivores (group TL 3.19) among named groups; the family's large-bodied members (Eleutheronema tetradactylum, Leptomelanosoma indicum) are placed separately with Large Benthic Carnivores by their larger size/TL - family not itself named in Table 1.
Eel/moray order; large benthic ambush-predator eel, not named in Table 1 but ecologically and trophically (TL ~3.9-4.4) closest to the demersal apex-predator guild of Large Benthic Carnivores.
Silver pomfret; "pomfrets" (Stromateidae, genus Pampus) is Table 1's explicit example for Med Benthic Carnivores.

CORRECTION to the inherited mapping. Photopectoralis bindus is the accepted name of Leiognathus bindus, member 51 of Grp10 Small Benthic Carnivores in the Bulletin 51 components-of-ecological-groupings table (PDF pp. 21-22) and one of the two species whose L-inf, P/B and Q/B the group account tabulates. Previously mapped to Small Benthopelagics.

Flathead grey mullet; mullets (Mugilidae) are benthic detritivore/omnivore grazers, not named in Table 1 but ecologically and trophically (TL 2.14-2.63) closest to the low-TL Benthic Omnivores guild (group TL 2.55).
Batoidea (skates/rays/sawfishes) is exactly the taxonomic scope of the model's Skates & Rays group.
Guitarfish family (batoid, order Rhinopristiformes); unambiguous fit to Skates & Rays.

Indian halibut (Psettodidae); a large predatory flatfish grouped with the "flounders" example by taxonomic order (Pleuronectiformes) even though its TL (4.39) runs well above the group's 3.19, since it is not Soleidae (the "soles" that map to Benthic Omnivores).
Greater lizardfish; "lizardfishes" is Table 1's explicit example for Large Benthic Carnivores.
Chacunda gizzard shad; Clupeidae, the family that itself defines the Clupeids group.
Mussel family; "bivalves" is Table 1's explicit example for Heterotrophic Benthos.

Giant trevally; Carangidae, but a large apex predatory reef jack/trevally (TL 3.8-4.5) rather than the small schooling "scad" niche Table 1 names for Carangidae under Small Benthopelagics - placed instead with the demersal apex-predator guild (Large Benthic Carnivores) by size, diet and TL.
Swimming crab family; Portunus and Charybdis, Table 1's explicit example genera for Crabs and lobsters, both belong to this family.
Whitefin wolf-herring; exact genus (Chirocentrus = "wolf herring") explicitly named in Table 1's Large Benthopelagics definition.
Spottail shark; exact genus (Carcharhinus) explicitly named in Table 1's Sharks definition.
Snapper family; Lutjanidae (snapper/jobfish family) - "jobfish" and "red snappers" are Table 1's explicit examples for Large Benthic Carnivores.
Goldstripe sardinella; "lesser sardines" (Sardinella spp) is Table 1's explicit example for Clupeids.
Silver sillago; small demersal sand-dwelling carnivore, SAU size class "Medium demersals" and TL (~3.25-3.33) closely matching Med Benthic Carnivores (group TL 3.19); family not named in Table 1.
Cobia; large solitary pelagic/benthopelagic piscivore, not one of Table 1's named examples but ecologically closest to the Large Pelagics apex-predator guild (TL 3.96 vs group TL 4.18).

Order-level flatfish record. The model splits flatfishes by feeding mode: the Malabar sole Cynoglossus macrostomus sits in Benthic Omnivores and the flounders Pseudorhombus arsius and P. natalensis in Med Benthic Carnivores per the Bulletin 51 components-of-ecological-groupings table (PDF pp. 21-22). Default catch-composition weights would be set by the croaker-dominated catch of Med Benthic Carnivores rather than by its flatfish members, so explicit weights are used instead, computed from this LME's own identified flatfish landings: Soleidae 1,764,086 t against Psettodes erumei, Bothus pantherinus and Bothidae 370,194 t, i.e. 0.83 sole-type to 0.17 flounder-type.
Yellowstriped goatfish; "goatfishes" (Mullidae) is Table 1's explicit example for Small Benthic Carnivores.
Javelin grunter; Haemulidae (grunt/sweetlips family), a demersal benthic-invertivore guild not named in Table 1, placed with Med Benthic Carnivores by ecology and TL (~3.3-4.0 vs group TL 3.19).

Grunt/sweetlips family; Haemulidae (grunt/sweetlips family), a demersal benthic-invertivore guild not named in Table 1, placed with Med Benthic Carnivores by ecology and TL (~3.3-4.0 vs group TL 3.19).
Rainbow sardine; exact common-name match to Table 1's explicit "rainbow sardines" example for Clupeids.
Jarbua terapon; "terapons" (Terapontidae) is Table 1's explicit example for Small Benthic Carnivores.
Genus explicitly named in Table 1's Tunas definition (Euthynnus, Thunnus, Auxis spp).
Orange-spotted grouper; Serranidae (grouper/rockcod family) - "rock cods" is Table 1's explicit example for Large Benthic Carnivores.
Bartail flathead; "flatheads" is Table 1's explicit example for Med Benthic Carnivores.
Grunter (genus); Haemulidae (grunt/sweetlips family), a demersal benthic-invertivore guild not named in Table 1, placed with Med Benthic Carnivores by ecology and TL (~3.3-4.0 vs group TL 3.19).

King soldier bream; Sparidae, but its TL (4.49) sits far closer to the apex demersal-predator guild of Large Benthic Carnivores (group TL 4.14) than to the rest of this workbook's lower-TL Sparidae, which cluster with Med Benthic Carnivores (group TL 3.19).
Dorab wolf-herring; exact genus (Chirocentrus = "wolf herring") explicitly named in Table 1's Large Benthopelagics definition.

Emperor (genus); Lethrinidae (emperor family), a demersal durophagous/piscivorous carnivore guild not named in Table 1 but ecologically parallel to the snapper/grouper apex reef-predator guild of Large Benthic Carnivores (mean TL ~3.7, group TL 4.14).
John's snapper; Lutjanidae (snapper/jobfish family) - "jobfish" and "red snappers" are Table 1's explicit examples for Large Benthic Carnivores.
White sardinella; matches Table 1's explicit "white sardine" example for Clupeids by common name and genus (Sardinella).
Granulated guitarfish (Rhinopristiformes, batoid); same family group as Table 1's explicit genus Rhynchobatus.

Filefish family; a close taxonomic relative of Balistidae (order Tetraodontiformes, Table 1's explicit "balistids") with similar benthic-invertivore ecology (TL 3.0 vs group 3.19), though not itself the named family.
Mangrove red snapper; Lutjanidae (snapper/jobfish family) - "jobfish" and "red snappers" are Table 1's explicit examples for Large Benthic Carnivores.
Arabian carpetshark (Orectolobiformes); a true shark, unambiguous fit under the model's clean shark/batoid split.
Cutlassfish/hairtail ("ribbonfish") family, explicit Table 1 example for Large Benthopelagics.
